newsitem.title: USA: Orphan Medical animal drug approved.
newsitem.headline: Orphan Medical animal drug approved.

text.p: Orphan Medical Inc said Tuesday the Center for Veterinary Medicine of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved its Antizol-Vet animal drug for marketing.
Antizol-Vet is an antidote for ethylene glycol poisoning in dogs. Ethylene glycol is a chemical component of antifreeze and coolants.
While assessments vary, Orphan Medical estimates that there are approximately 10,000 dogs in the United States that could benefit from this antidote therapy each year.
If administered early enough, Antizol-Vet can prevent the severe clinical consequences of ethylene glycol ingestion, including death, it added.
Antizol-Vet, also known as fomepizole, is exclusively available through W.A. Butler Co.

Orphan Medical said it is also studying fomepizole as an antidote for ethylene glycol and methanol poisoning in humans. The company plans to submit the marketing application for human use of fomepizole this year.
